title: Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) Master Specification v1.1
description: Canonical master specification of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), which models the universe as a thermodynamic-information system driven by energy-flow and entropy gradients. It formalizes three base layers—EFC-S (structure/halos), EFC-D (energy-flow dynamics), and EFC-C0 (entropy–information mapping)—and fixes baseline fields, notation, and equations to enable unambiguous higher-level models and simulations.

energy_flow_potential.description: Baseline local energy-flow potential coupling mass density and dimensionless entropy; high density and low entropy yield large flow capacity.

low_entropy_anchor.description: Definition of a low-entropy anchor region A that seeds halo formation in EFC-S.

halo_profiles_parametrized.description: Joint mass-density and entropy halo profiles parameterized by scale radii r_s and r_c with shape functions f and g defining halo classes.

mass_density_definition.description: Standard definition of mass density used within the EFC-D layer.

key_results.main_finding: Establishes a compact, explicit core specification for EFC across structure, dynamics, and entropy–information mapping with Ef = \rho(1 - S) as the central field.

sealed_predictions.statement: At fixed mass density, measurable information-capacity proxies decrease approximately linearly with increasing entropy, consistent with I(S) ∝ (1 − S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Cross-population studies of astrophysical systems (e.g., galactic environments) where proxies for information capacity (phase-space granularity, coherent structure fraction) are measured versus independently estimated entropy.

kill_criteria: KC1: Galaxy rotation curves and strong/weak lensing maps cannot be jointly reproduced using EFC-D with observed baryonic density ρ(x) and plausible entropy fields S(x) (no dark matter allowed), across a representative sample of galaxies and clusters.
KC2: Empirical dynamics at fixed mass density show no suppression with increasing entropy (i.e., no dependence on the (1 − S) factor), contradicting Ef = ρ(1 − S).

KC3: The observed expansion history H(z) from SNe Ia, BAO, and CMB cannot be matched by any EFC-D flow/entropy solution without introducing an explicit dark-energy term, while ΛCDM fits the same data.
KC4: Independent entropy estimators for the same systems yield mutually incompatible S(x) fields that lead to irreconcilable EFC predictions beyond stated uncertainties.
KC5: The EFC-D evolution equations imply violations of energy conservation or the second law in closed systems when confronted with laboratory/astrophysical tests.

KC6: The predicted monotonic decrease of information capacity with entropy (I ∝ 1 − S at fixed ρ) is robustly falsified by observations showing equal or higher information capacity in higher-entropy states after controlling for density.
